ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC = 45^\circ$. $F$ is the intersection point of altitudes $AD$ and $BE$, $AC = \sqrt{5}$, $BD = 2$. What is the length of segment $DF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AD$ and $BE$ are altitudes of $\triangle ABC$,\\
it follows that $\angle ADB = \angle ADC = \angle BEC = 90^\circ$.\\
Thus, $\angle C + \angle DAC = 90^\circ$; $\angle C + \angle DBF = 90^\circ$.\\
This means $\angle DAC = \angle DBF$.\\
Since $\angle ABC = 45^\circ$,\\
it implies $\angle DAB = 45^\circ$.\\
Hence, $\angle ABC = \angle DAB$.\\
Therefore, $DA = DB$.\\
In $\triangle ADC$ and $\triangle BDF$,\\
\[\left\{ \begin{array}{l} \angle ADC = \angle BDF \\ DA = DB \\ \angle DAC = \angle DBF \end{array} \right.\]\\
Thus, $\triangle ADC \cong \triangle BDF$ (ASA).\\
Therefore, $AC = BF = \sqrt{5}$.\\
In right $\triangle BDF$, with $\angle BDF = 90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $BD^2 + DF^2 = BF^2$.\\
Given $BD = 2$, and $BF = \sqrt{5}$,\\
it concludes $DF = \boxed{1}$.
